statusText: Yellow / WATCH. Tail 22% sits inside the watch band and below the block threshold, while Stress 55% stays elevated on a 2007-high Treasury selloff and Brent above $103.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH. A narrow danger window is flagged from 19:30 to 20:15 UTC across the closing auction and the immediate post-close repricing. Outside that window the observed price path retains two-way character, with the index holding roughly 100 points above its session low.
headline: Nasdaq-100 pullback stays orderly into the close as the 10-year yield retraces from its 2007 high
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades at 30,452.59, down 279.81 points (-0.91%) from a 30,732.40 previous close, inside a 30,353.88-30,706.23 session range. Roughly half an hour before the cash close the index sits about 100 points above the session low rather than at it, QQQ is 2.6 points off its own low at 740.81, and VIX at 14.96 (+5.28%) is below its 15.45 session high. The driver remains the bond market: the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.13% intraday, the highest since 2007, and has since eased to 5.11-5.12%, with the 2-year at 4.91% (+15.5 basis points) and the 30-year at 5.40%. September flash PMIs surprised strongly to the upside, the composite rising to 58.4 from 56.0 with services at 58.7, the strongest private-sector expansion since July 2021, while input costs rose at the fastest pace since October 2022. Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said risks to the inflation target have increased while labour-market risks have receded, signalling support for a further increase at the 26-28 October meeting and lifting October hike pricing to roughly 70%. Energy is the second channel: Brent trades at $103.41 (+4.19%) and WTI at $92.61 (+2.31%) after a cargo vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran's president used his UN General Assembly address to restate conditions for reopening the waterway. Semiconductors are the weakest complex, with SOXX at 563.99 (-1.53%) though about seven points above its own session low. The combination of a sustained bounce off the lows, a VIX retreating from its high and a 10-year yield that has stopped making new session highs is why elevated Stress is not accompanied by a blocking Tail score.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours opened with a trend-up regime carrying Tail near 20% into the 22 September US close, then decayed steadily through the Asian and European sessions to a Tail low of 10-12% in a normal dominant mode. Conditions changed from roughly 12:00 UTC on 23 September as the Treasury selloff accelerated: Tail reached 25% in a trend-down mode at 14:00 UTC, the only blocking hour of the window, before settling into a 22-24% mixed regime for the rest of the US session as the index retraced off its lows while Stress climbed into the mid-to-high 50s.
outlookSummary: The immediate focus is the 19:30-20:15 UTC window spanning the closing auction and the first post-close prints, the narrow stretch where late-session continuation risk concentrates; conditional Tail stays inside the watch band there rather than crossing the block threshold, because the index has produced a sustained bounce off its session low, VIX has retreated from its high and the 10-year yield has stopped making new session highs. Beyond the close, conditional Tail decays through the Globex and Asian sessions into the mid teens, with Strait of Hormuz headline flow the main overnight gap channel and the Tokyo open the first test of whether the 2007-high US yield transmits globally. Risk rebuilds on 24 September around Initial Jobless Claims at 12:30 UTC, peaking near 23% at the 13:30 UTC cash open, since on the inherited calibration a scheduled release raises stress and forecast dispersion before it raises tail. The projection returns to the high teens by the end of the horizon on the base case that the hawkish repricing is absorbed in an orderly, two-way fashion.

Rate-driven but two-way.
